messages.subject: Profiling TMB model for improving speed
parts:
Hi friends,

Anyone have resources for profiling the TMB model code? I can find profilers for generic C++ code, but it's not clear to me how to fit my TMB model wrapped in R functions into that framework.

Thanks!
Sam

messages.author: db75de8828a1b4ea
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Profiling TMB model for improving speed
parts:
I found this blog post, which I just attempted to use on my TMB model:

http://minimallysufficient.github.io/r/programming/c++/2018/02/16/profiling-rcpp-packages.html

I added the line they suggest to my global Makevars file, and created the cpp file in my wd, using sourceCpp("start_profiler.cpp") to load the functions. Followed the instructions for starting the profiler, running my model, stopping the profiler, and getting output saved.

I'm probably gonna write something more in-depth for how to bend this framework around to a more TMB related approach later (and perhaps outside of a package structure), but so far so good!

Sam

messages.author: 16c32bb3268768fd
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Profiling TMB model for improving speed
parts:
Thanks Sam and Grant for the resources! 

I've also used Intel VTunes to profile my TMB code on a Windows machine. In the VTunes Configure Analysis Section, I attach the R process using the PID. I look this up on the Task Manager by right clicking on the R (or Rstudio) process and selecting 'Go to details'. The correct .exe will be highlighted with its PID. The downside to this method is that I have to manually start the profiler, switch back to R and run the code, then manually stop the profiler when the script is finished.
